_why: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for 'which subagent transcripts are the pipeline's own exhaust'.
Exhaust = a transcript whose entire content is a brief WE wrote, about work already
ingested. Extracting it is not merely wasteful, it is corrupting: workers obey the
embedded brief as their own task, the contract's rules land in the brain as Nick's
decisions, and — the real killer — extraction spawns workers whose transcripts become
new pending evidence, so 'nothing pending after close' is unreachable. Hub refresh has
the same shape: refreshing a hub indexed the refresh run as new evidence ON that hub,
so it re-drifted immediately (observed 3x in 2 days on sentinel-security-review).
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS AT ALL (2026-07-28). The filter lived as a regex inside
extract-pending.sh listing exact brief-opening phrases, while the briefs themselves were
written by hand from prose directives in a DIFFERENT file. Only the extraction producer
was ever told its required phrase; the hub-refresh producer was never told any phrase, so
each close invented one. Three phrasings shipped across closes and the regex matched none:
it wanted 'Compiled-truth refresh', they all said 'Compiled-truth HUB refresh'. One word.
22 of 42 pending files were leaked exhaust, silently, for two days — exactly what the
regex's own comment warned would happen if anyone reworded that first line.
Two phrase lists that must agree, kept in two files, is a drift generator. So: one file,
read by the detector AND quoted by every dispatch directive. Adding a producer means

_role: Prose-independent backstop. A phrase list can only ever describe briefs already written;
the NEXT reworded brief leaks before anyone notices. These match on what a worker
transcript unavoidably CONTAINS — the pipeline's own file paths — so a producer that
invents new wording is still caught. All terms in a group must appear in the head.
Kept narrow enough that a genuine session discussing the pipeline is not swallowed:
the terms must co-occur in the first 1500 chars, i.e. inside the brief itself.
Makes the NEXT drift loud instead of silent. If several pending files share a near
identical brief opening, that is a producer whose phrase stopped matching — the exact
failure this file was created after. The detector prints EXHAUST-LEAK-SUSPECT; it does
NOT auto-exclude, because auto-excluding on repetition would let a legitimately
repetitive class of real evidence vanish unread.
MACHINE-READABLE SELF-IDENTIFICATION, added 2026-08-28 on core-business's design (bus #5837).
Every mechanism above matches PROSE the producer happened to write. That is the standing defect:
'only the EXTRACTION producer was ever told its required phrase — the hub-refresh producer was
told none, invented three phrasings, and this regex matched none of them'. business hit the same
thing from the other side — it hand-wrote three sentinel-code briefs in its own wording and each
became a new unrecognised opening — and named the asymmetry that makes it unfixable downstream:
only the WRITER Core can register a phrase, so the Core producing the leak structurally cannot
close it.
A token is not paraphrasable. You can reword 'Brain-graph extraction worker' by accident; you
cannot accidentally reword CORE-PIPELINE-EXHAUST/v1. So a producer declares WHAT IT IS instead of
the detector guessing from how it opened.
SCOPE — THIS IS RECOGNITION, NOT POLICY, AND THE DISTINCTION IS LOad-BEARING. The marker changes
HOW a pipeline worker is identified. It does NOT change WHICH producers are excluded, and it must
never be stamped on a Sentinel, census, or research brief. extract-pending.sh:145 records why:
C12's measured evidence is that those carry real signal and still flow through the gate, and
62-89% of subagent graph nodes are unique. Stamping one would delete knowledge and silently
reverse Nick's 2026-07-25 extractor-as-gate decision.
Phrases and structural_signatures STAY. They cover every brief written before this existed, and
removing them would re-leak the entire back catalogue.
dispatch_marker._where: Emit anywhere in the first 1500 chars of the worker brief — the detector reads only the head.
